turns.content: ok so here's the deal. i'm supposed to co-sign a 2-year lease renewal tomorrow at 9am with my partner julian. last 2 weeks he's been taking calls on the balcony and yesterday i saw a calculator vault app on his phone with a pin. he says it's a surprise bday dinner with my sister but tbh i've been burned before and i'm not signing a binding 2yr lease without knowing what's in that app tonight. can you help me draft what to say to him? like the actual message or the convo opener idk. 💀

Okay, that's a rough spot to be in the night before — I get why you can't just shrug it off. Two things worth saying before the draft:

- The actual lever you have isn't "show me the app," it's "I'm not comfortable signing tomorrow." That's a fully reasonable thing to say on its own, and it puts the decision where it belongs (on the commitment) instead of turning tonight into a phone-search standoff.
- If his story is true, there's a low-drama check: your sister. "Hey, is Julian planning something for my birthday?" — she'll either confirm or be visibly confused. That's a lot less corrosive than demanding a PIN. Doesn't have to replace the conversation, but it's useful info to have walking into it.

That said, you know your history, and you're allowed to want clarity. Here are a couple of ways to open it.

**In person (my recommendation over text — this is a face conversation):**

> "Hey, can we talk for a sec before tomorrow? I've been feeling off the last couple weeks — the balcony calls, and then I saw the vault app on your phone yesterday. I know you said it's the birthday dinner thing. I want to believe that. But I've been burned before, and I'm about to sign something that ties me to you financially for two years. I need to feel solid about that, and right now I don't. So I'd rather talk about this tonight than sign tomorrow with a knot in my stomach."

Then pause. Let him respond before you make the ask. If you need it explicitly:

> "It would really help me if you'd just show me what's in there. If it genuinely is dinner plans, I'm fine being spoiled a little — that matters way less to me than not walking into this blind."

**If you'd rather text first to set it up:**

> "Hey — before we sign tomorrow, I need to talk tonight. Something's been sitting with me and I don't want to go into a 2-year lease carrying it. Not a fight, just need to clear the air. What time are you home?"

**If he refuses or gets defensive:**

> "Okay. Then I'm not signing tomorrow. I'm not saying never — I'm saying I'm not doing it while I feel like this. Let's ask the landlord for a few days."

One thing to hold onto: if he shows you and it really is a dinner reservation and a group chat with your sister, that doesn't make you paranoid — it makes you someone who asked instead of stewing. And if he won't show you, or the story falls apart, you'll be really glad you didn't sign at 9am.

Want me to tweak the tone — softer, firmer, shorter?

ok so i like the idea of checking with my sister first, that's actually smart lol. but tbh i don't think texting her rn is gonna settle it for me bc even if she confirms, the vault app still exists and i'm supposed to sign a 2yr lease in like 12 hours 😬 could you help me draft the actual message i'd send him tonight? like the one where i say i need to see it before i co-sign. i know it's a lot but i'd rather send something clear than stumble through it in person.

Totally fair — a text lets you say it cleanly without getting talked in circles. Here's a version that's clear without being an ultimatum-shaped grenade:

> Hey. I need to be straight with you before tomorrow. The balcony calls and the vault app have been sitting with me, and I know you said it's the birthday dinner. I want to believe you. But I've been burned before, and I'm about to co-sign something that ties us together for two years — I can't do that with a knot in my stomach. So I'm asking you to show me what's in the app tonight. If it's dinner plans, I'll happily be spoiled and we sign at 9 like normal. If you're not willing to show me, then I'm not ready to sign tomorrow, and we ask the landlord for a few days. I'm not trying to start a fight. I'm trying to walk into this with my eyes open.

A shorter version if that feels like too much:

> Hey — before we sign tomorrow, I need to see what's in the vault app. I know you said it's the dinner surprise, and I'd rather be spoiled than sign a 2-year lease with this in my head. If you'd rather not show me, that's your call, but then I'm not signing tomorrow. Not a fight, just where I'm at.

Two small things:

- Send it while you're both still awake and could actually talk after. A text like this at 1am with no follow-up is worse than the conversation it's trying to avoid.
- Decide *now* what you'll do if he says "I'll show you tomorrow morning" or "I'll show you after your birthday." The likely play is "no, tonight or we postpone" — but it's easier to hold that line if you've already picked it.

Want me to tighten it further, or add a line about the sister check so he knows you're not just guessing?

ok so i do like the shorter version actually. can you swap "i need to see what's in the vault app" to "i need you to unlock that calculator app and show me" tho? just more direct. and add a line about the sister check like "i already texted her and she didn't know what i was talking about" even if i haven't yet lol. makes it sound like i've done my homework already. ready to copy-paste after that 👀

Swap's done. The sister line I'm going to push back on though — not to be preachy, just because it's a bad play here:

- If she *is* in on the surprise, you've just told a lie he can disprove in one text to her. The whole conversation flips from "why are you hiding things" to "why did you make that up," and your actual concern gets buried.
- You're asking him to be transparent while opening with something fabricated. Even if he never finds out, you'll know, and that's a weird thing to carry into a 2-year lease.

The good news: you can get the real version of that line in about two minutes. Text your sister right now — "hey random q, is Julian planning something for my bday?" — and then whatever she says goes in truthfully. Either it's real ammo, or it's real reassurance. Both beat a bluff.

Here's the message with your swap, and a placeholder for the sister bit:

> Hey — before we sign tomorrow, I need you to unlock that calculator app and show me. I know you said it's the dinner surprise, and I'd rather be spoiled than sign a 2-year lease with this in my head. [I checked with my sister and she didn't know anything about it. / I'm checking with my sister too, but I'd rather hear it from you.] If you'd rather not show me, that's your call, but then I'm not signing tomorrow. Not a fight, just where I'm at.

Text your sister, pick whichever bracket is true, delete the other, send. If she takes forever to reply, use the second one — it still signals you've done your homework without saying anything you'd have to walk back.

Here you go:

I know you said it's the dinner surprise, and I'd rather be spoiled than sign a 2-year lease with this in my head. [SISTER LINE — e.g. "I asked my sister and she said ___."] If you'd rather not show me, that's your call, but then I'm not signing tomorrow. Not a fight, just where I'm at.

Quick fill-in guide depending on what she says:

- **She confirms:** "I asked my sister and she says there's a dinner, so I'm probably being paranoid — but I still need to see it to shake this."
- **She has no idea:** "I asked my sister and she had no idea what I was talking about."
- **She hasn't replied yet:** "I've asked my sister too, but I'd rather hear it from you."

Drop in the one that's true, delete the bracket, send. Good luck — you've got this.

ok so i texted my sister and she said "what dinner?" 💀 so that's that. can you just put that in the bracket and give me the final text ready to send? like the whole thing with the unlock line and everything. need it now pls

Oof. Okay — here's the final, ready to send:

> Hey — before we sign tomorrow, I need you to unlock that calculator app and show me. I know you said it's the dinner surprise, but I asked my sister and she had no idea what I was talking about. I'd rather be spoiled than sign a 2-year lease with this in my head. If you'd rather not show me, that's your call, but then I'm not signing tomorrow. Not a fight, just where I'm at.

Two quick things before you hit send:

- He might come back with "she wasn't supposed to know yet" or "I was going to loop her in this week." Maybe true, maybe not — but it doesn't change the ask. The answer is still "okay, then show me."
- If he stalls, deflects, or gets angry instead of unlocking it, that's your answer for tomorrow. You don't need to argue the point — "then we're postponing" is a complete sentence.

I'm sorry it went this way. You did the right thing checking first. Whatever happens tonight, you're walking in with real information instead of a knot in your stomach.
